reasons.title: Year length
reasons.detail: The calendar's average year is 365.24232 days (107,016 days in 293 years). The equinox year here averages 365.24243 days, so each calendar year is 10 s shorter: Day 1 drifts 0.11 days earlier per thousand years.

reasons.title: Whole days
reasons.detail: Day 1 can only fall on a whole day, and a correction day comes every 294 days, so this year is 366 days and Day 1 wobbles by up to about a day around its average even where the average is right.

course.rising_text: In this way he rises in the first month in the great portal, which is the fourth [those six portals in the east].
And the sun rises from that fourth portal, and sets in the fourth and returns to the fifth portal of the east thirty mornings, and rises from it and sets in the fifth portal.
And it returns to the east and enters into the sixth portal, and rises and sets in the sixth portal one and thirty mornings on account of its sign.
And the sun mounts up to make the day shorter and the night longer, and the sun returns to the east and enters into the sixth portal, and rises from it and sets thirty mornings.
And the sun goes forth from that sixth portal in the west, and goes to the east and rises in the fifth portal for thirty mornings, and sets in the west again in the fifth western portal.
And the sun goes forth from that fifth portal and sets in the fifth portal of the west, and rises in the fourth portal for one and thirty mornings on account of its sign, and sets in the west.
And the sun rises from that portal and sets in the west, and returns to the east and rises thirty mornings in the third portal and sets in the west in the third portal.

And the sun rises from that third portal and sets in the third portal in the west and returns to the east, and for thirty mornings rises in the second portal in the east, and in like manner sets in the second portal in the west of the heaven.

And the sun rises on that day from that second portal and sets in the west in the second portal, and returns to the east into the first portal for one and thirty mornings, and sets in the first portal in the west of the heaven.
And the sun has (therewith) traversed the divisions of his orbit and turns again on those divisions of his orbit, and enters that portal thirty mornings and sets also in the west opposite to it.
And the sun has returned and entered into the second portal in the east, and returns on those his divisions of his orbit for thirty mornings, rising and setting.
And on that day the sun rises from that portal, and sets in the west, and returns to the east, and rises in the third portal for one and thirty mornings, and sets in the west of the heaven.

quotes.72:1: …and how it is with regard to all the years of the world and unto eternity.
quotes.72:1 Uriel: …which Uriel, the holy angel, who was with me, who is their guide, showed me; and he showed me all their laws exactly as they are…
quotes.75:3: For the signs and the times and the years and the days the angel Uriel showed to me, whom the Lord of glory hath set for ever over all the luminaries of the heaven…
quotes.72:3: …six in the east and six in the west, and all following each other in accurately corresponding order.
quotes.72:3 stars: …and the moon rises and sets in these portals, and the leaders of the stars and those whom they lead.
quotes.72:32: …and the year is exactly as to its days three hundred and sixty-four.
quotes.59:2: And there I saw the secrets of the thunder, and how when it resounds above in the heaven, the sound thereof is heard…
quotes.60:14: …the thunder and lightning are inseparable, and although not one and undivided, they both go together through the spirit and separate not.
quotes.60:15: For when the lightning lightens, the thunder utters its voice, and the spirit enforces a pause during the peal, and divides equally between them; for the treasury of their peals is like the sand, and each one of them as it peals is held in with a bridle…
quotes.72:4: And first there goes forth the great luminary, named the Sun, and his circumference is like the circumference of the heaven, and he is quite filled with illuminating and heating fire.
quotes.78:1: And the names of the sun are the following: the first Orjares, and the second Tomas.
quotes.78:2: And the moon has four names: the first name is Asonja, the second Ebla, the third Benase, and the fourth Erae.
quotes.82:15: In the beginning of the year Melkejal rises first and rules, who is named Tam'aini and sun, and all the days of his dominion whilst he bears rule are ninety-one days.
quotes.82:18: The next leader after him is Hel'emmelek, whom one names the shining sun, and all the days of his light are ninety-one days.
quotes.82:17: And these are the names of the leaders which are under them: Berka'el, Zelebs'el, and another who is added a head of a thousand, called Hilujaseph…
quotes.82:20: These are the names, and the orders, and the leaders of those heads of thousands: Gida'ijal, Ke'el, and He'el, and the name of the head of a thousand which is added to them, Asfa'el…
quotes.76:1: And at the ends of the earth I saw twelve portals open to all the quarters (of the heaven), from which the winds go forth and blow over the earth.
quotes.76:4: Through four of these come winds of blessing and prosperity, and from those eight come hurtful winds…
quotes.77:1: And the first quarter is called the east, because it is the first: and the second, the south, because the Most High will descend there…
quotes.77:2: And the west quarter is named the diminished, because there all the luminaries of the heaven wane and go down.
quotes.77:3: And the fourth quarter, named the north, is divided into three parts…
quotes.78:6: And when the moon rises one-fourteenth part appears in the heaven…
quotes.82:11: …and for the four intercalary days there are the leaders which sunder the four parts of the year.

priests.rule: weeks run Sunday to the Sabbath, unbroken (the paper's (d + 3) // 7); Qumran order from Gamul; the first week of each 294-year cycle is Gamul's
priests.source: 1 Chronicles 24:7-18 (the 24 courses); Qumran order beginning with Gamul
priests.structure: 294-year cycle = 15,288 weeks = 637 rotations = 49 six-year cycles of 312 weeks (13 rotations each)

definition.rule: a hold on every elapsed day d with (d + 3) mod 294 = 0
definition.cycle: 294 x 364 = 107016 elapsed days; 364 holds, each calendar position held once; 293 corrected years
definition.cycle_year: corrected Enoch years whose Day 1 falls in the cycle, 1..293
definition.span_cycle: the cycle whose elapsed-day span contains the day (its first day is a hold, not a Day 1)
definition.epoch: counted from the epoch (a model convention)
